IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
PARVIN KUMAR JAIN v. ANJU JAIN
Citation: 2024 INSC 961 | Civil Appeal No. 14210 of 2024
Bench: Hon'ble Justice Vikram Nath & Hon'ble Justice Prasanna B. Varale
Date of Judgment: December 10, 2024
JUDGMENT & LEGAL PRINCIPLES
This judgment addresses key issues surrounding matrimonial disputes, dissolution of marriage on grounds of
irretrievable breakdown under Article 142 of the Constitution, and the independent nature of financial
maintenance claims under Sections 24 and 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
FACTUAL BACKGROUND
The parties were married for over two decades but had lived separately since 2004 due to irreconcilable
differences. Multiple litigations including divorce petitions, maintenance applications, and child custody disputes
were pending across various forums.
RATIO DECIDENDI & COURT FINDINGS
1. Article 142 & Irretrievable Breakdown: Recognizing that the marital bond was beyond repair after 20 years of
separation, the Supreme Court exercised its plenary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to
grant a decree of divorce to do complete justice.
2. Survival of Maintenance Claims: The Court established that maintenance claims under Sections 24 and 26 of
the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, are independent statutory remedies. The withdrawal or dismissal of the
underlying matrimonial suit does not automatically terminate or negate pending claims for spousal or child
maintenance.
3. One-Time Settlement & Financial Provision: The Court awarded a consolidated one-time settlement of Rs. 6
Crores (comprising Rs. 5 Crores towards permanent alimony for the wife and Rs. 1 Crore for higher education
and maintenance of the son).
ORDER & DISPOSITION
The Supreme Court dissolved the marriage, directed payment of the quantified permanent settlement within the
specified timeline, and disposed of all connected proceedings.
